title: M/S P.S.S. Taxcon Sadikpur v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Shekhar B. Saraf, J.; Dr. Yogendra Kumar Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; Clause 6.5 authority directed to decide the pending representation.
headnote: A writ challenging disconnection of supply, with a representation still pending, was disposed of by directing the Clause 6.5 authority to treat that representation as one under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and to pass a reasoned order after hearing, without any merits determination of the disconnection or restoration.
facts: The petitioner, M/S P.S.S. Taxcon Sadikpur, challenged under Article 226 the order dated 31 December 2024 by which respondent no. 5 disconnected electricity to its unit, and sought a mandamus directing restoration of the connection. Counsel submitted that, raising those grievances, the petitioner had already filed a representation before the respondent-authority on 27 December 2024, but that representation had not yet been decided.

holding_units.holding: Where disconnection of supply is challenged and a representation remains undecided, the authority dealing with Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is directed to treat that representation as one under Clause 6.5 and to pass a reasoned order in accordance with law after hearing the consumer, within four weeks; the writ is disposed of without deciding the merits of disconnection or restoration.

not_decided.point: validity of the 31 December 2024 disconnection and entitlement to restoration
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the disconnection or restoration on merits, remitting the pending representation to the Clause 6.5 authority.
